title: millionco/react-doctor
description: Your agent writes bad React. This catches it Your agent writes bad React, this catches it. One command scans your codebase and outputs a 0 to 100 health score with actionable diagnostics. Works with Next.js, Vite, and React Native. See it in action → Install Run this at your project root: npx -y react-doctor@latest . You'll get a score (75+ Great, 50 to 74 Needs work, under 50 Critical) and a list of issues across state & effects, performance, architecture, security, accessibility, and dead code. Rules toggle automatically based on your framework and React version. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/07cc88d9-9589-44c3-aa73-5d603cb1c570 Install for your coding agent Teach your coding agent React best practices so it stops writing the bad code in the first place. npx -y react-doctor@latest install You'll be prompted to pick which detected agents to install for. Pass --yes to skip prompts. Works with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, OpenCode, and 50+ other agents. GitHub Actions A composite action ships with this repository. Drop it into .github/workflows/react-doctor.yml: name: React Doctor on: pull_request: push: branches: [main] permissions: contents: read pull-requests: write # required to post PR comments jobs: react-doctor: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v5 with: fetch-depth: 0 # required for `diff` - uses: millionco/react-doctor@main with: diff: main github-token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }} When github-token is set on pull_request events, findings are posted (and updated) as a PR comment. The action also exposes a score output (0–100) you can use in subsequent steps. Inputs: directory, verbose, project, diff, github-token, fail-on (error / warning / none), offline, node-version. See action.yml for full descriptions. Prefer not to add a marketplace action? The bare npx form works too: - run: npx -y react-doctor@latest --fail-on warning Configuration Create a react-doctor.config.json in your project root: { "ignore": { "rules": ["react/no-danger", "jsx-a11y/no-autofocus"], "files": ["src/generated/**"], "overrides": [ { "files": ["components/modules/diff/**"], "rules": ["react-doctor/no-array-index-as-key", "react-doctor/no-render-in-render"] }, { "files": ["components/search/HighlightedSnippet.tsx"], "rules": ["react/no-danger"] } ] } } Three nested keys, three layers of granularity — pick the narrowest one that fits: ignore.rules silences a rule across the whole codebase. ignore.files silences every rule on the matched files (use sparingly — it loses coverage for unrelated rules). ignore.overrides silences only the listed rules on the matched files, leaving every other rule active. This is what you want when a single file (or glob) legitimately needs an exemption from one or two rules but should still be scanned for everything else. You can also use the "reactDoctor" key in package.json. CLI flags always override config values. React Doctor respects .gitignore, .eslintignore, .oxlintignore, .prettierignore, and linguist-vendored / linguist-generated annotations in .gitattributes. Inline // eslint-disable* and // oxlint-disable* comments are honored too. If you have a JSON oxlint or eslint config (.oxlintrc.json or .eslintrc.json), its rules get merged into the scan automatically and count toward the score. Set adoptExistingLintConfig: false to opt out. Optional companion plugins When the following ESLint plugins are installed in the scanned project (or hoisted in your monorepo), React Doctor folds their rules into the same scan. Both are listed as optional peer dependencies — install only what you want. Plugin Adds Namespace eslint-plugin-react-hooks (v6 or v7) The React Compiler frontend's correctness rules — fired when a React Compiler is detected in the project. react-hooks-js/* eslint-plugin-react-you-might-not-need-an-effect (v0.10+) Complementary effects-as-anti-pattern rules (no-derived-state, no-chain-state-updates, no-event-handler, no-pass-data-to-parent, …) that run alongside React Doctor's native State & Effects rules. effect/* Inline suppressions // react-doctor-disable-next-line react-doctor/no-cascading-set-state useEffect(() => { setA(value); setB(value); }, [value]); When two rules fire on the same line, you have two equivalent options. Comma-separate the rule ids on a single comment: // react-doctor-disable-next-line react-doctor/rerender-state-only-in-handlers, react-doctor/no-derived-useState const [localSearch, setLocalSearch] = useState(searchQuery); Or stack one comment per rule directly above the diagnostic. Stacked comments are honored as long as nothing but other react-doctor-disable-next-line comments sits between them and the target line: // react-doctor-disable-next-line react-doctor/rerender-state-only-in-handlers // react-doctor-disable-next-line react-doctor/no-derived-useState const [localSearch, setLocalSearch] = useState(searchQuery); A code line between stacked comments breaks the chain: only the comment immediately above the diagnostic (and any contiguous react-doctor-disable-next-line comments stacked on top of it) is honored. If a comment looks adjacent but the rule still fires, run react-doctor --explain <file:line> — it reports whether a nearby suppression was found, what rules it covers, and why it didn't apply. Block comments work inside JSX: {/* react-doctor-disable-next-line react/no-danger */} <div dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html }} /> For multi-line JSX, putting the comment immediately above the opening tag covers the entire attribute list (matching ESLint convention). Lint plugin (standalone) The same rule set ships as both an oxlint plugin and an ESLint plugin, so you can wire it into whichever lint engine your project already runs. oxlint in .oxlintrc.json: { "jsPlugins": [{ "name": "react-doctor", "specifier": "react-doctor/oxlint-plugin" }], "rules": { "react-doctor/no-fetch-in-effect": "warn", "react-doctor/no-derived-state-effect": "warn", }, } ESLint flat config: import reactDoctor from "react-doctor/eslint-plugin"; export default [ reactDoctor.configs.recommended, reactDoctor.configs.next, reactDoctor.configs["react-native"], reactDoctor.configs["tanstack-start"], reactDoctor.configs["tanstack-query"], ]; The full rule list lives in oxlint-config.ts. CLI reference Usage: react-doctor [directory] [options] Options: -v, --version display the version number --no-lint skip linting --no-dead-code skip dead code detection --verbose show every rule and per-file details (default shows top 3 rules) --score output only the score --json output a single structured JSON report -y, --yes skip prompts, scan all workspace projects --full skip prompts, always run a full scan --project <name> select workspace project (comma-separated for multiple) --diff [base] scan only files changed vs base branch --staged scan only staged files (for pre-commit hooks) --offline skip telemetry --fail-on <level> exit with error on diagnostics: error, warning, none --annotations output diagnostics as GitHub Actions annotations --explain <file:line> diagnose why a rule fired or why a suppression didn't apply --why <file:line> alias for --explain -h, --help display help When a suppression isn't working, --explain <file:line> (or its alias --why <file:line>) reports what the scanner sees at that location, including why a nearby react-doctor-disable-next-line didn't apply. The diagnosis distinguishes the common failure modes — adjacent comment for a different rule (use the comma form), a code line between the comment and the diagnostic (the chain is broken), or no nearby suppression at all. The same hint surfaces inline with --verbose for every flagged site, and in --json output as diagnostic.suppressionHint, so a single scan doubles as a suppression audit without a separate flag. --json produces a parsable object on stdout with all human-readable output suppressed. Errors still produce a JSON object with ok: false, so stdout is always a valid document. Config keys Key Type Default ignore.rules string[] [] ignore.files string[] [] ignore.overrides { files, rules? }[] [] lint boolean true deadCode boolean true verbose boolean false diff boolean | string failOn "error" | "warning" | "none" "none" customRulesOnly boolean false share boolean true offline boolean false textComponents string[] [] rawTextWrapperComponents string[] [] respectInlineDisables boolean true adoptExistingLintConfig boolean true ignore.tags string[] [] entryFiles string[] [] textComponents is the broad escape hatch for rn-no-raw-text — list components that themselves behave like React Native's <Text> (custom Typography, NativeTabs.Trigger.Label, etc.) and the rule will treat them as text containers regardless of what their children look like. rawTextWrapperComponents is the narrower option for components that are not text elements but safely route string-only children through an internal <Text> (e.g. heroui-native's Button, which stringifies its children and renders them through a ButtonLabel). Listed wrappers suppress rn-no-raw-text only when their children are entirely stringifiable. A wrapper with mixed children — e.g. <Button>Save<Icon /></Button> — still reports because the wrapper can't safely route raw text alongside a sibling JSX element. ignore.tags suppresses entire categories of rules by tag. For example, "tags": ["design"] disables all opinionated design rules (gradient text, pure black backgrounds, side tab borders, default Tailwind palettes). Available tags: "design". entryFiles tells the dead-code detector about files that are executed directly but not imported (test runner configs, eval scripts, CLI entry points). These are forwarded to knip as additional entry points. Example: "entryFiles": ["scripts/*.ts", "evalite.config.ts"]. If your project already has a knip.json, those entry points are respected automatically. offline skips the score API call and calculates the score locally. Automatically enabled in CI environments (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, CircleCI). Set true in config to always score locally. Scoring The health score formula: 100 - (unique_error_rules x 1.5) - (unique_warning_rules x 0.75). Key details: The score counts unique rules triggered, not total instances. Fixing 49 of 50 no-barrel-import violations does not change the score; fixing all 50 removes the 0.75 penalty for that rule. Error-severity rules cost 1.5 points each. Warning-severity rules cost 0.75 points each. Category breakdowns shown in the output are for display only and do not weight the score. Run --verbose to see which exact rules contributed to the score and how the penalty was computed. Score labels: 75+ is Great, 50 to 74 is Needs work, under 50 is Critical. Scores may decrease across releases as new rules are added. Each new rule that fires in your codebase introduces an additional penalty. This is expected — it means the tool is catching more issues, not that your code got worse. Pin to a specific react-doctor version in CI if you need stable scores across upgrades. Diff and staged modes React Doctor can scan only changed files instead of the full project: --diff [base] scans files changed vs a base branch. Auto-detects main/master, or pass an explicit branch: --diff develop. Also available as a config key: "diff": true or "diff": "develop". --staged scans only files in the git staging area (index). Designed for pre-commit hooks — materializes staged file contents into a temp directory so the scan reflects exactly what will be committed. --full forces a full scan, overriding any diff value in config or CLI. When on a feature branch without explicit flags, you'll be prompted: "Only scan changed files?" This prompt is suppressed in CI, --json mode, and non-interactive environments. --staged and --diff cannot be combined. Both modes skip dead-code detection (knip needs the full project to detect unused files). Agent and CI integration React Doctor detects 50+ coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, OpenCode, Windsurf, and more) and adapts its behavior automatically: Install for agents: npx react-doctor@latest install writes agent-specific rule files (SKILL.md, AGENTS.md, .cursorrules) into your project so agents learn React best practices. JSON output: --json produces a structured JsonReport on stdout. Errors still produce a valid JSON document with ok: false. Use --json-compact for minimal whitespace. Score-only output: --score outputs just the numeric score (0-100), useful for threshold checks in agent loops. GitHub Actions annotations: --annotations emits ::error / ::warning format for inline PR annotations. Exit codes: --fail-on error (default) exits non-zero when error-severity diagnostics are found. Use --fail-on warning or --fail-on none to tune CI gating. Programmatic API: import { diagnose } from "react-doctor/api" for direct integration in scripts and automation. In CI environments, prompts are automatically skipped and scoring runs locally (offline mode). Node.js API import { diagnose, toJsonReport, summarizeDiagnostics } from "react-doctor/api"; const result = await diagnose("./path/to/your/react-project"); console.log(result.score); // { score: 82, label: "Great" } or null console.log(result.diagnostics); // Diagnostic[] console.log(result.project); // detected framework, React version, etc. diagnose accepts a second argument: { lint?: boolean, deadCode?: boolean }. const report = toJsonReport(result, { version: "1.0.0" }); const counts = summarizeDiagnostics(result.diagnostics); react-doctor/api re-exports JsonReport, JsonReportSummary, JsonReportProjectEntry, JsonReportMode, plus the lower-level buildJsonReport and buildJsonReportError builders. See packages/react-doctor/src/api.ts for the full types. Leaderboard Top React codebases scanned by React Doctor, ranked by score. Resources & Contributing Back Want to try it out? Check out the demo. Looking to contribute back? Clone the repo, install, build, and submit a PR. git clone https://github.com/millionco/react-doctor cd react-doctor pnpm install pnpm build node packages/react-doctor/bin/react-doctor.js /path/to/your/react-project Find a bug? Head to the issue tracker. License React Doctor is MIT-licensed open-source software.
tldr: millionco 发布 React Doctor，一键扫描 React 代码库并输出健康评分与诊断
objective_summary: millionco 发布 React Doctor 工具，可通过 npx 命令扫描 React 项目（支持 Next.js、Vite、React Native），输出 0-100 的健康评分及状态与副作用、性能、架构、安全、可访问性、死代码等维度的诊断。
key_logic_flow: React Doctor 提供 npx react-doctor@latest . 命令一键扫描代码库，输出 0-100 的健康评分（75+ 为优秀，50-74 为需改进，50 以下为严重），并附带可操作的诊断列表。
评分公式为 100 - (唯一错误规则数 × 1.5) - (唯一警告规则数 × 0.75)，计数的是触发的唯一规则而非总实例数。
工具支持 npx react-doctor install 为 Claude Code、Cursor、Codex 等 50 多种编码智能体安装最佳实践规则。
提供 GitHub Actions composite action，可在 PR 事件中自动发布诊断注释，并暴露 score 输出供后续步骤使用。
支持多层忽略配置（全局规则、全局文件、文件级规则覆写），兼容 .gitignore 等同级忽略文件，并识别 inline disable 注释。
同一规则集同时以 oxlint 插件和 ESLint 插件形式发布，可选集成 eslint-plugin-react-hooks v6/v7 和 eslint-plugin-react-you-might-not-need-an-effect 的规则。

impact_score.reason: React Doctor 是针对 AI 编码智能体时代的一个精准工具——它解决的是 'AI 写出烂 React 代码' 这一真实痛点，且提供了评分公式、CI 集成、50+ 编码智能体规则安装等完整工作流。然而本质上它是一个打包了 React 最佳实践的 lint 工具，其技术架构（oxlint/ESLint 双插件、忽略层级配置）是成熟的工程手段而非突破性创新。短期内对 React 开发者群体有明显实用价值，能改变团队代码审查流程，但不会引发范式转移。评分 5.5 反映了 '重要且实用的产品发布' 定位，介于日常更新与行业变革之间。

developer_sentiment.primary_focus: 规则集的实际准确性与误报率——是否能在不产生大量噪音的前提下真正捕获 AI 生成的典型反模式代码

hype_assessment.reason: 项目 README 以实操为主，直接给出 CLI 命令、配置文件示例、CI 集成代码和评分公式，没有使用 '颠覆'、'革命性' 等 PR 滥用词汇。标题 'Your agent writes bad React, this catches it' 直白务实，技术细节密度高，属于实打实的产品文档风格而非概念炒作。

domain_disruption.technical_innovation: 核心创新在于将 React 最佳实践规则集同时编译为 oxlint 插件和 ESLint 插件，实现单一规则源的双引擎分发；此外，通过 npx react-doctor install 向 50+ 编码智能体注入项目级规则文件的方式，是 AI 辅助编码时代工具链集成的一种新范式。规则本身（如 no-cascading-set-state、no-derived-useState）并无理论突破，但规则的组织、评分公式（100 - 唯一错误规则数 × 1.5 - 唯一警告规则数 × 0.75）和多层忽略配置体系设计精良。
domain_disruption.business_model: 开源工具本身不直接变现，但 millionco 可借此强化其在 React 性能优化领域的品牌认知，为其商业产品（如 million.js 虚拟 DOM 优化库）和企业咨询服务导流。同时，GitHub Actions 集成和编码智能体规则安装功能锁定了开发者工作流入口，未来存在向团队协作面板或 SaaS 监控平台演进的商业化路径。

compound_value.reason: CoT强制推理四维度：(1)市场时机【强】——AI编码Agent（Claude Code/Cursor/Codex等50+种）大规模普及，Agent生成React代码普遍存在状态管理、副作用、性能等反模式，React Doctor精准卡位「AI-human代码质量交汇点」，解决真实且增长的痛点。(2)分发策略【创新】——npx react-doctor install可向50+种编码Agent注入最佳实践规则，以Agent为分发渠道而非直接营销开发者，获客成本极低且覆盖路径独特；GitHub Actions composite action嵌入CI/CD流水线形成工作流粘性。(3)护城河深度【偏浅】——核心规则基于React社区已知最佳实践（React Compiler规则、effects-as-anti-pattern等），无专有IP壁垒；有足够工程资源的团队可在数周内复制核心功能。健康评分公式虽形成可引用的度量标准，但不构成排他性壁垒。唯一差异化护城河是Agent集成生态的先发优势和规则库的持续维护能力。(4)变现路径【模糊】——代码检查工具历史上鲜有成为大规模独立商业的先例（ESLint/SonarQube对比），更可能成为Vercel/Next.js等平台的内置功能或被吸收。millionco需以此作为楔子产品扩展为React全生命周期开发工具平台方能突破估值天花板。综合：有成为细分赛道基础设施的潜力，但需持续验证商业化路径与护城河深度，当前评分5.5。

competitive_casualty: 传统React代码审计/咨询服务商
独立React Lint规则集维护项目
React专项培训课程
market_opportunities: AI 编码质量护栏赛道正在成形：React Doctor 的「扫描→评分→诊断」模式可复用到 Vue、Svelte、Angular 等其他前端框架，创业团队可快速推出竞品或垂直领域（如金融级 React 合规扫描）的定制版本，利用 oxlint + ESLint 双插件策略实现最大化生态覆盖
「代码健康分」概念衍生出企业级 SaaS 机会：将 0-100 评分体系产品化为跨项目、跨团队的仪表盘与趋势看板，结合 AI 编码智能体的规则注入能力，向工程效能（Engineering Productivity）平台方向演进，可对标 SonarQube 的 React 专项版
个人开发者可将 React Doctor 的规则体系作为 React 最佳实践的体系化学习路径，逐条理解每条规则的动机与反模式场景，快速提升 React 代码审查与架构设计能力，尤其适合从 Vue/Angular 转 React 或初中级开发者系统补齐知识盲区

risk_matrix.technological: React 范式演进风险：当前规则体系基于客户端 React 经典模式（useEffect、useState），若 React Server Components 成为主流范式，大量现有规则将失效或需重构；oxlint 生态成熟度不及 ESLint，若 Vite 团队调整 oxlint 战略方向，双插件策略的 oxlint 侧将面临维护成本激增

risk_matrix.ethical: 评分体系存在隐性偏见风险：健康评分公式（唯一错误规则数 × 1.5 + 唯一警告规则数 × 0.75）对大型单体仓库天然不利，可能诱导团队为追求高分而过度拆分组件或禁用规则；AI 智能体规则注入功能若被企业强制推行，可能限制开发者编码风格自由，形成「工具暴政」；安全维度的诊断可能赋予团队虚假的安全合规信心
additional: 供应商锁定风险：millionco 作为小型开源公司（核心产品 Million.js 尚未主流），若项目后继乏力或商业方向转变，已深度集成 React Doctor 的 CI/CD 流水线与 AI 智能体工作流将面临迁移成本
误报疲劳风险：静态分析工具的规则覆盖面越广，误报率越难控制；若团队未建立有效的忽略配置文化，大量误报将导致告警疲劳，反而降低整体代码质量关注度
供应链安全风险：npx 一键执行远程代码的模式（npx react-doctor@latest .）若 millionco 的 npm 账户或 GitHub 仓库遭入侵，攻击者可注入恶意扫描逻辑窃取源码或环境变量

title: mattpocock/skills
description: Skills for Real Engineers. Straight from my .claude directory. Skills For Real Engineers My agent skills that I use every day to do real engineering - not vibe coding. Developing real applications is hard. Approaches like GSD, BMAD, and Spec-Kit try to help by owning the process. But while doing so, they take away your control and make bugs in the process hard to resolve. These skills are designed to be small, easy to adapt, and composable. They work with any model. They're based on decades of engineering experience. Hack around with them. Make them your own. Enjoy. If you want to keep up with changes to these skills, and any new ones I create, you can join ~60,000 other devs on my newsletter: Sign Up To The Newsletter Quickstart (30-second setup) Run the skills.sh installer: npx skills@latest add mattpocock/skills Pick the skills you want, and which coding agents you want to install them on. Make sure you select /setup-matt-pocock-skills. Run /setup-matt-pocock-skills in your agent. It will: Ask you which issue tracker you want to use (GitHub, Linear, or local files) Ask you what labels you apply to ticks when you triage them (/triage uses labels) Ask you where you want to save any docs we create Bam - you're ready to go. Why These Skills Exist I built these skills as a way to fix common failure modes I see with Claude Code, Codex, and other coding agents. #1: The Agent Didn't Do What I Want "No-one knows exactly what they want" David Thomas & Andrew Hunt, The Pragmatic Programmer The Problem. The most common failure mode in software development is misalignment. You think the dev knows what you want. Then you see what they've built - and you realize it didn't understand you at all. This is just the same in the AI age. There is a communication gap between you and the agent. The fix for this is a grilling session - getting the agent to ask you detailed questions about what you're building. The Fix is to use: /grill-me - for non-code uses /grill-with-docs - same as /grill-me, but adds more goodies (see below) These are my most popular skills. They help you align with the agent before you get started, and think deeply about the change you're making. Use them every time you want to make a change. #2: The Agent Is Way Too Verbose With a ubiquitous language, conversations among developers and expressions of the code are all derived from the same domain model. Eric Evans, Domain-Driven-Design The Problem: At the start of a project, devs and the people they're building the software for (the domain experts) are usually speaking different languages. I felt the same tension with my agents. Agents are usually dropped into a project and asked to figure out the jargon as they go. So they use 20 words where 1 will do. The Fix for this is a shared language. It's a document that helps agents decode the jargon used in the project. Example Here's an example CONTEXT.md, from my course-video-manager repo. Which one is easier to read? BEFORE: "There's a problem when a lesson inside a section of a course is made 'real' (i.e. given a spot in the file system)" AFTER: "There's a problem with the materialization cascade" This concision pays off session after session. This is built into /grill-with-docs. It's a grilling session, but that helps you build a shared language with the AI, and document hard-to-explain decisions in ADR's. It's hard to explain how powerful this is. It might be the single coolest technique in this repo. Try it, and see. Tip A shared language has many other benefits than reducing verbosity: Variables, functions and files are named consistently, using the shared language As a result, the codebase is easier to navigate for the agent The agent also spends fewer tokens on thinking, because it has access to a more concise language #3: The Code Doesn't Work "Always take small, deliberate steps. The rate of feedback is your speed limit. Never take on a task that’s too big." David Thomas & Andrew Hunt, The Pragmatic Programmer The Problem: Let's say that you and the agent are aligned on what to build. What happens when the agent still produces crap? It's time to look at your feedback loops. Without feedback on how the code it produces actually runs, the agent will be flying blind. The Fix: You need the usual tranche of feedback loops: static types, browser access, and automated tests. For automated tests, a red-green-refactor loop is critical. This is where the agent writes a failing test first, then fixes the test. This helps give the agent a consistent level of feedback that results in far better code. I've built a /tdd skill you can slot into any project. It encourages red-green-refactor and gives the agent plenty of guidance on what makes good and bad tests. For debugging, I've also built a /diagnose skill that wraps best debugging practices into a simple loop. #4: We Built A Ball Of Mud "Invest in the design of the system every day." Kent Beck, Extreme Programming Explained "The best modules are deep. They allow a lot of functionality to be accessed through a simple interface." John Ousterhout, A Philosophy Of Software Design The Problem: Most apps built with agents are complex and hard to change. Because agents can radically speed up coding, they also accelerate software entropy. Codebases get more complex at an unprecedented rate. The Fix for this is a radical new approach to AI-powered development: caring about the design of the code. This is built in to every layer of these skills: /to-prd quizzes you about which modules you're touching before creating a PRD /zoom-out tells the agent to explain code in the context of the whole system And crucially, /improve-codebase-architecture helps you rescue a codebase that has become a ball of mud. I recommend running it on your codebase once every few days. Summary Software engineering fundamentals matter more than ever. These skills are my best effort at condensing these fundamentals into repeatable practices, to help you ship the best apps of your career. Enjoy. Reference Engineering Skills I use daily for code work. diagnose — Disciplined diagnosis loop for hard bugs and performance regressions: reproduce → minimise → hypothesise → instrument → fix → regression-test. grill-with-docs — Grilling session that challenges your plan against the existing domain model, sharpens terminology, and updates CONTEXT.md and ADRs inline. triage — Triage issues through a state machine of triage roles. improve-codebase-architecture — Find deepening opportunities in a codebase, informed by the domain language in CONTEXT.md and the decisions in docs/adr/. setup-matt-pocock-skills — Scaffold the per-repo config (issue tracker, triage label vocabulary, domain doc layout) that the other engineering skills consume. Run once per repo before using to-issues, to-prd, triage, diagnose, tdd, improve-codebase-architecture, or zoom-out. tdd — Test-driven development with a red-green-refactor loop. Builds features or fixes bugs one vertical slice at a time. to-issues — Break any plan, spec, or PRD into independently-grabbable GitHub issues using vertical slices. to-prd — Turn the current conversation context into a PRD and submit it as a GitHub issue. No interview — just synthesizes what you've already discussed. zoom-out — Tell the agent to zoom out and give broader context or a higher-level perspective on an unfamiliar section of code. prototype — Build a throwaway prototype to flesh out a design — either a runnable terminal app for state/business-logic questions, or several radically different UI variations toggleable from one route. Productivity General workflow tools, not code-specific. caveman — Ultra-compressed communication mode. Cuts token usage ~75% by dropping filler while keeping full technical accuracy. grill-me — Get relentlessly interviewed about a plan or design until every branch of the decision tree is resolved. handoff — Compact the current conversation into a handoff document so another agent can continue the work. write-a-skill — Create new skills with proper structure, progressive disclosure, and bundled resources. Misc Tools I keep around but rarely use. git-guardrails-claude-code — Set up Claude Code hooks to block dangerous git commands (push, reset --hard, clean, etc.) before they execute. migrate-to-shoehorn — Migrate test files from as type assertions to @total-typescript/shoehorn. scaffold-exercises — Create exercise directory structures with sections, problems, solutions, and explainers. setup-pre-commit — Set up Husky pre-commit hooks with lint-staged, Prettier, type checking, and tests.

tldr: AiToEarn 是一个开源 AI Agent 一站式内容变现平台，支持在 14+ 社交平台上自动创作、分发和变现内容。
objective_summary: yikart 开发的开源平台 AiToEarn 于 2025 年 2 月首次发布，通过 AI Agent 在抖音、TikTok、YouTube 等 14 个社交平台实现内容自动创作、分发、互动运营和变现，支持网页直接使用、MCP 协议集成、Docker 部署等多种方式。
key_logic_flow: AiToEarn 是由 yikart 开发的开源一站式内容变现平台，核心目标是通过 AI Agent 自动化帮助一人公司、创作者和企业在全球主流平台实现内容变现。
平台覆盖 14 个社交平台：抖音、小红书、快手、B站、视频号、微信公众号、TikTok、YouTube、Facebook、Instagram、Threads、Twitter(X)、Pinterest、LinkedIn。
提供四种核心 Agent 能力：Monetize（内容交易市场，支持 CPS/CPE/CPM 结算）、Publish（一键多平台分发+日历排期）、Engage（自动点赞/评论/品牌监测）、Create（AI 自动生成视频和图文内容）。
支持五种使用方式：直接网页访问（aitoearn.cn/aitoearn.ai）、OpenClaw 插件集成、MCP 协议接入（兼容 Claude/Cursor 等 AI 助手）、Docker 一键部署、源码开发模式。
项目版本演进从 2025 年 2 月首个开源版本到 2026 年 4 月的 OpenClaw 集成，经历了出海多平台支持、AI Agent 集成、线下商户推广方案、内容交易市场上线等重要里程碑。
平台提供中国版和国际版双环境，通过 MCP 和 SSE 两种协议对外暴露 API，支持第三方 AI 工具的无缝集成。

impact_score.reason: 该开源项目通过AI Agent整合了14个社交平台的内容创作、分发与变现链路，并引入MCP协议实现跨AI助手集成，在创作者经济细分领域有明确的实用价值。但其本质是应用层整合（社交API+AI生成+任务市场），并未带来AI底层技术突破或行业范式转移，短期冲击力主要局限在内容创作工具赛道和一人公司群体，属于'重要但非颠覆'的产品发布。

developer_sentiment.primary_focus: AI自动生成内容的真实质量与原创性存疑，14个平台的内容合规性（尤其抖音/小红书等强审核平台）和API稳定性是落地关键风险

hype_assessment.reason: 文章使用了'超级AI智能Agent''一站式平台'等营销包装词汇，但同时也附带了清晰的版本迭代记录、四种核心Agent能力的具体定义和五种使用方式的详细配置说明，属于有实体的适度包装，并非空洞概念炒作

domain_disruption.technical_innovation: 将MCP协议引入内容变现场景，实现AI Agent与多平台社交API的标准化交互，使Claude、Cursor等第三方AI工具可直接操控内容发布与互动运营；同时将跨境双环境（中国版+国际版）的14个社交平台API统一抽象为一套Agent接口，降低了多平台运营的工程复杂度
domain_disruption.business_model: 构建了一个内容交易市场（CPS/CPE/CPM三种结算），将商家推广需求商品化并匹配给AI驱动的创作者，形成'商家出钱—Agent创作—平台分发—按效果结算'的自动化变现闭环，可能重塑微型创作者的经济模式

compound_value.reason: CoT 投资逻辑：(1) 核心价值主张是成为 MCP 生态中连接 AI Agent 与社交平台的中间件层，这是差异化定位而非又一个内容工具——通过 MCP 协议，AiToEarn 可被 Claude、Cursor 等任何 AI 助手直接调用，形成「Agent 分发→平台执行→变现结算」的闭环，具备基础设施潜力；(2) 但长期复利效应存在三重不确定性：第一，社交平台 API 生态高度不确定（Twitter/X 多次封杀第三方工具是前车之鉴），平台方随时可收紧权限或推出官方竞品；第二，开源模式导致代码层护城河薄弱，竞争对手可低成本复制核心能力；第三，AI 生成内容正面临各平台日益严格的监管（如 TikTok 的 AI 标签要求），内容变现的合规风险在上升；(3) 加分项在于 CPS/CPE/CPM 结算体系一旦形成双边网络效应（商家↔创作者），就具有交易平台的粘性，但当前阶段尚处于冷启动期。综合判断：3-5 年内有约 40% 概率成为 MCP Agent 生态的关键中间件节点，但不足以称为行业基石，属「需持续验证的潜力型基础设施」。

key_beneficiaries: OpenClaw (龙虾 — 通过 AiToEarn 插件获得内容变现能力)
competitive_casualty: 传统社媒管理 SaaS (Hootsuite/Buffer 等)
MCN 机构（多头签约+人工运营模式受冲击）
内容代运营公司（人力密集型服务被 Agent 替代）
各社交平台原生创作者工具（抖音创作者平台等）
传统联盟营销平台（CPS 类）
market_opportunities: 基于 AiToEarn 的 MCP 协议集成能力，开发者可为其客户构建定制化 AI 内容助手插件，嵌入 Claude Desktop、Cursor 等主流 AI 工具生态，提供垂直行业（如餐饮、美业、房产）的一站式多平台内容代运营 SaaS 服务。
一人公司（OPC）和微型创作者经济正在爆发，可围绕 AiToEarn 的开源架构开发细分领域的内容变现模板市场（如探店视频模板、产品测评模板），通过 CPS 分佣模式实现模板创作者与使用者的双边收益。
该平台的 CPS/CPE/CPM 三种结算模式提供了广告效果归因的数据闭环，数据分析师和增长黑客可基于此构建跨平台 ROI 追踪看板，帮助企业量化「AI 生成内容 → 多平台分发 → 实际转化」的全链路效果。

risk_matrix.regulatory: 平台支持中国版（aitoearn.cn）和国际版（aitoearn.ai）双环境运营，涉及跨境数据传输和内容合规的双重监管风险。中国版需遵守《数据出境安全评估办法》对用户数据的跨境流动限制；国际版在欧盟市场需符合 GDPR 对自动化决策和用户画像的合规要求；此外，AI 生成内容在抖音、小红书等平台可能触发平台方的 AI 内容标识政策，面临限流或下架风险。
risk_matrix.technological: 核心能力深度依赖第三方 AI 模型（Grok、Veo、Seedance、Nano Banana 等）和 14 个社交平台的非公开 API，任一模型服务中断或平台封禁自动化发布行为都可能导致核心功能瘫痪。平台通过 Relay 服务借用官方 OAuth 凭据完成授权，这种架构存在单点故障风险和凭据被撤销的技术隐患。此外，MCP 协议仍处于早期发展阶段，生态稳定性存在不确定性。
risk_matrix.competitive: 各社交平台正在自建 AI 创作工具（如抖音即创、YouTube Create），未来可能通过官方工具替代第三方自动化方案。内容变现赛道已有 Buffer、Hootsuite 等成熟竞品，且 Notion、Figma 等协作工具也在向 AI Agent 方向延伸，巨头入场可能挤压开源项目的生存空间。项目由个人开发者主导，团队规模和资源有限，难以与资本支持的商业产品打持久价格战。
risk_matrix.ethical: 平台的 Engage Agent 支持自动点赞、评论、关注等批量运营行为，本质上是在制造虚假互动和社会化媒体操纵，违反多数平台的服务条款。AI 批量生成内容可能导致社交媒体信息流被低质量 AI 内容污染，降低用户体验。内容交易市场中以 CPS/CPE/CPM 结算的推广任务，缺乏对虚假流量和刷量行为的有效甄别机制，可能滋生灰色产业链。此外，AI 自动生成的视频和图文内容存在肖像权、版权和深度伪造的潜在风险。
additional: 依赖个人开源维护的可持续性风险：项目核心由 yikart 个人维护，缺乏基金会或企业背书，存在停更、弃坑或商业化转型后闭源的可能性，采纳方需评估长期技术依赖成本。
支付与结算合规风险：CPS/CPE/CPM 三种结算涉及创作者与商家之间的资金流转，平台作为撮合方可能触及支付牌照监管红线，尤其是在中国版涉及人民币结算的场景下。

tldr: FadCam：FadSec Lab 推出的开源隐私优先 Android 多媒体套件，支持后台录像、行车记录仪、录屏、直播和远程控制。
objective_summary: anonfaded 在 GitHub 上发布 FadCam，一款基于 Android 的开源多媒体应用，集成行车记录仪、屏幕录制、本地网络直播和远程摄像头控制功能，强调无广告、无数据收集、无追踪的隐私保护设计，已获得多家科技媒体关注。
key_logic_flow: FadCam 是 FadSec Lab 套件中的 Android 开源项目，由 anonfaded 开发和维护。
该应用提供四大核心功能：后台视频录制（支持息屏录制）、行车记录仪模式（分段 MP4 格式防损坏）、屏幕录制（带标注工具）、以及本地网络直播与远程摄像头控制。
应用采用 Material Design 设计，提供 7 种以上主题（含 AMOLED 模式）和 15 种以上自定义图标。
隐私方面明确声明：100% 无广告、无数据收集、无追踪，并包含从最近应用列表中隐藏的隐私选项。
可设置定时录制、支持地理标记水印（基于 OpenStreetMap 的 Nominatim 逆地理编码），以及通过硬件按键映射触发快捷操作。
提供 Patreon 付费的 FadCam Pro 终身版，并接受社区贡献和 GitHub Issue/PR 协作。

impact_score.reason: 该事件为 Android 开源多媒体工具（FadCam）的发布与社区传播，与 AI 行业无直接关联。其功能涵盖行车记录仪、屏幕录制、局域网直播等，属于成熟移动应用领域的增量创新，不涉及 AI 模型、训练范式、推理框架或数据工程等 AI 核心议题，对 AI 行业不产生可测量的短期冲击力。

developer_sentiment.primary_focus: 隐私优先的开源 Android 多媒体工具的功能完整性和实用性，与 AI 领域无直接交集

hype_assessment.reason: 项目 README 以功能清单和技术特性描述为主，未使用'颠覆''革命性'等 PR 滥用词汇，宣传较为克制务实，仅通过 Patreon 提供付费版本，无夸大炒作痕迹。

domain_disruption.technical_innovation: 无 — 该工具属于 Android 客户端应用开发范畴，使用 ExoPlayer 等成熟组件，不涉及 AI 技术架构或算法层面的突破。
domain_disruption.business_model: 无 — Patreon 付费 Pro 版本为开源项目的常规变现路径，与 AI SaaS 生态或 API 经济无关联。

compound_value.reason: FadCam 是开源 Android 终端应用，虽有多家科技媒体背书和隐私优先的差异化定位，但从 VC 视角看，其复利效应极弱：① 无网络效应——用户增长不带来产品价值提升；② 无数据护城河——隐私优先设计反而排除了数据飞轮；③ 变现路径单一——仅依靠 Patreon 付费的 Pro 终身版，客单价低且无法规模化；④ 竞争壁垒低——功能组合（后台录像、行车记录仪、录屏、直播）均可被复制，大厂原生系统（Android 自带录屏、Pixel 系行车记录仪功能）正在逐步内置类似能力；⑤ 开源协议降低了商业独占性。3-5 年后大概率仍是小众隐私工具，难以成为行业基石。评分 3.5，处于'昙花一现'与'细分赛道基础设施'之间的下沿。

key_beneficiaries: 隐私导向的开源 Android 社区
competitive_casualty: 广告驱动的 Android 录屏/行车记录仪应用
付费订阅制 Android 工具应用
低端车载摄像头硬件厂商（手机替代效应）
中国出海工具类 App（含广告 SDK 追踪的应用）
market_opportunities: 开源隐私工具的双轨变现模式（GitHub 开源免费版 + Patreon 终身 Pro 版）已被 FadCam 初步验证，独立开发者可参考此路径，在文件管理、相册、输入法、笔记等高频 Android 工具品类中复制隐私优先的差异化打法，通过社区口碑裂变降低获客成本
废旧 Android 手机再利用场景正在形成新市场——FadCam 将旧手机转化为行车记录仪或家用 CCTV 的软件方案，创业者可围绕"旧设备即硬件"思路，开发针对特定场景（宠物监控、婴儿监护、店铺安防）的专用刷机包或定制 ROM，搭配低功耗优化和远程管理面板实现产品化
本地优先（local-first）工具生态正在形成独立赛道，FadCam 的"全本地、零云上传"架构验证了用户对数据主权的需求，建议关注与其互补的工具链机会，如本地加密备份、设备间 P2P 同步、端侧 AI 视频摘要生成等可集成或捆绑的增值模块

risk_matrix.regulatory: 视频录制应用在各国面临差异化法律限制：背景息屏录制在部分司法管辖区可能触犯窃听/偷拍相关法律（如未经同意的隐蔽录制），应用的"道德使用"免责声明法律效力存疑；地理标记功能若嵌入视频元数据，在 GDPR 管辖区可能涉及个人数据处理合规问题，即使数据仅存储在本地也存在灰色地带
risk_matrix.technological: Android 平台每次大版本更新可能收紧后台执行限制和存储权限（Scoped Storage），核心功能如息屏录制存在被系统策略阻断的风险；ExoPlayer 已被 Google 弃用并转向 Media3，技术栈面临迁移压力；项目为单人维护（anonfaded），存在关键人风险，长期可持续性存疑
risk_matrix.competitive: Android 原生功能持续覆盖 FadCam 能力版图（AOSP 已有屏幕录制、Google 相机集成车载模式）；小米、OPPO、OnePlus 等国产厂商在定制 ROM 中内置行车记录仪和屏幕录制功能，挤压第三方工具空间；Proton、Signal 等隐私品牌若横向扩展至多媒体工具领域将形成品牌降维打击
risk_matrix.ethical: 应用内置的"从最近应用列表隐藏"功能本质上支持隐蔽录制，存在被滥用于偷拍、跟踪、职场监控等场景的显著风险；尽管开发者声明禁止非道德使用，但技术上无任何防护机制阻止此类行为；地理位置水印功能在未经被拍摄者同意时可能侵犯他人隐私权
additional: 商业模式脆弱性：Patreon 单一收入渠道受平台政策变更和创作者经济波动影响，项目缺乏多元化收入来源，长期维护动力可能衰减
品牌声誉连带风险：若 FadCam 被关联至负面社会事件（如偷拍案件），FadSec Lab 旗下其他产品（FadCrypt 等）将遭受品牌污染，"隐私优先"的定位可能反转为"隐私滥用工具"的舆论危机

description: Implement a ChatGPT-like LLM in PyTorch from scratch, step by stepBuild a Large Language Model (From Scratch) This repository contains the code for developing, pretraining, and finetuning a GPT-like LLM and is the official code repository for the book Build a Large Language Model (From Scratch). In Build a Large Language Model (From Scratch), you'll learn and understand how large language models (LLMs) work from the inside out by coding them from the ground up, step by step. In this book, I'll guide you through creating your own LLM, explaining each stage with clear text, diagrams, and examples. The method described in this book for training and developing your own small-but-functional model for educational purposes mirrors the approach used in creating large-scale foundational models such as those behind ChatGPT. In addition, this book includes code for loading the weights of larger pretrained models for finetuning. hype_assessment.reason: 教程内容扎实，十六章系统覆盖从理论到RL训练的全流程，提供完整代码和视频课程，未使用'颠覆''革命性'等夸张修辞。虽然标题强调'Agent元年'有一定宣传色彩，但项目本体以教学内容交付而非概念炒作为核心，社区贡献精选和4万Star证明了其实质价值。

domain_disruption.technical_innovation: 无底层技术突破，但系统性整合了ReAct、Plan-and-Solve、Reflection等经典范式实现、MCP/A2A通信协议解析、以及从SFT到GRPO的Agentic-RL训练实战，形成了目前中文社区最完整的Agent全栈知识地图，其自研HelloAgents框架（V1.0.0）以OpenAI原生API为基础提供了轻量化教学参考实现。
domain_disruption.business_model: 采用CC BY-NC-SA 4.0开源协议完全免费，以社区驱动的内容共建模式运营，通过降低Agent开发人才门槛对整个AI应用生态产生正向外部性——为Dify、Coze等低代码平台和LangGraph等框架培养潜在用户与贡献者，形成人才供给侧的基础设施效应。

compound_value.reason: Hello-Agents 是中文 AI 社区中罕见的全栈 Agent 教育基础设施项目。其长期复利价值体现在三个层面：(1) 开发者网络效应——4万 Star 的社区基础已形成自增强的学习者-贡献者飞轮，社区精选贡献机制进一步加速内容沉淀；(2) 标准化学科体系——五大部分十六章覆盖从理论到 Agentic-RL 训练的全栈知识，有望成为中文 Agent 开发者的「标准课程」，3-5 年后仍将是新人入门首选；(3) 人才管道效应——该项目直接为整个 Agent 生态输送熟练开发者，间接推动上层应用爆发。但作为 CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 协议下的完全免费项目，直接价值捕获路径模糊，商业变现依赖 Datawhale 能否将社区影响力转化为企业培训、咨询服务或平台化产品。续作《从零开始训练智能体》若落地，可向模型训练层延伸影响力。综合来看，属于「强生态价值、弱直接变现」型基础设施，评分 7.0。

competitive_casualty: 商业 AI Agent 教育/培训平台
闭源 Agent 开发平台（依赖用户锁定而非开放标准）
付费 AI 课程内容商（同类内容免费后失去定价权）
低质量 AI 营销号/内容贩售者（项目主动水印防御）
market_opportunities: 该教程预计将批量培养数万名具备AI Native Agent全栈构建能力的开发者，企业可提前布局Agent人才招聘与内部培训体系，抢占Agent应用落地的人才红利
教程中自研HelloAgents框架结合Agentic-RL训练（SFT→GRPO）的完整教学链路，为垂直行业（金融、医疗、法律）提供了一条「领域微调+自定义Agent」的商业化路径，创业者可基于此模式开发行业专用智能体解决方案
教程对MCP、A2A等多Agent通信协议的深度覆盖，预示着跨Agent协作的标准化需求正在形成，中间件与互操作平台的创业窗口正在打开

risk_matrix.regulatory: 教程采用CC BY-NC-SA 4.0许可协议，明确禁止商业使用，企业若直接基于教程内容开发商业产品存在版权合规风险；此外Agent自主决策能力的大规模普及可能加速各国对AI Agent的监管立法（如欧盟AI Act对高风险Agent的分类要求）
risk_matrix.technological: Agent领域技术迭代极快（如MCP协议、Agentic-RL方法论仍在快速演进），教程中教授的具体框架和范式可能在12-18个月内过时；配套的HelloAgents自研框架尚未经过生产环境验证，存在架构债务风险
risk_matrix.competitive: 该教程大幅降低了Agent开发的门槛和成本，可能导致市场短期内涌入大量同质化的Agent产品，加剧价格竞争；同时大厂（如OpenAI、Google）可能通过内置Agent能力直接挤压第三方Agent框架的生存空间
risk_matrix.ethical: 教程教授从零构建自主Agent的完整能力，可能被恶意行为者用于开发自动化网络攻击、大规模虚假信息传播或社交操纵Agent；教程中关于Agent自进化（Self-Evolution）的内容若被滥用，可能产生超出设计者预期的危险行为
additional: 知识安全风险：该教程完整覆盖了从理论到训练的Agent全链路知识，相当于将Agent构建能力「开源民主化」，可能被敌对国家或组织用于快速建立AI Agent研发能力
社区依赖风险：教程质量高度依赖Datawhale社区的核心维护者（尤其是项目负责人陈思州），若核心贡献者流失，教程的持续更新和技术演进可能停滞
